audit_notes: Parameters are plausible. Checks: (1) sqrt(Kx) = 8.9 um (sqrt(Kx)+ = 2.35), sqrt(Kz) = 1.4 um (0.37), sqrt(Ky) = 1.2 um (0.32): below the Kelvin-Helmholtz onset sqrt(Ky)+ about 0.4 reported in DNS, so the drag-reducing regime is plausible. (2) An anisotropy Kx/Kz = 40 cannot be reached with aligned fibre mats (about 2); it needs the proposed geometry of streamwise channels under a perforated sheet with no spanwise connection, which is manufacturable by lamination. (3) Channel Reynolds number inside the skin: u_Darcy about tau_w*sqrt(Kx)/mu scale 100*8.9e-6/1.2e-3 = 0.74 m/s at the interface decaying within sqrt(Kx); Re_pore = 1025*0.74*9e-6/1.2e-3 about 6, still in the Darcy/Brinkman regime. (4) Structural: a 100 um silicone or PU skin under 100 Pa shear and 100 kPa hydrostatic pressure is fine if the perforated sheet is supported every 50-100 um; channel collapse under fender loads is a local damage risk. (5) Model: the virtual-origin offset (sqrt(Kx) - sqrt(Kz)) times the anisotropy_efficiency 0.7 is used as an effective Navier slip length (5.3e-6 m, b+ = 1.4) on an equivalent laminar Couette gap H = 1.2e-4 m that reproduces the 100 Pa smooth-wall shear. This first-order model gives about 4 %; the log-law shift estimate is about 8 %. (6) Not captured and dominant in practice: biofilm clogging of the channels within weeks, which turns the skin into a rough wall. Baseline: the impermeable smooth hull (anisotropy_efficiency = 0).
